An instruction that uses R4 as a source operand, store datum, or address base transfers its contents from the register file into the memory address/data backbone. The implemented dependency runs through `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_short -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.mdb_out_nxt -> openMSP430.eu_mdb_out`. Probing `openMSP430.eu_mdb_out` during that transaction exposes R4 directly for a move/store or reveals a deterministic address/data function of R4. The observation discloses all or part of the confidential R4 value and repeated chosen instructions can resolve otherwise masked bits.

When the instruction decoder selects R4 as `reg_src` or `reg_dest`, the execution unit presents its value to the ALU operand network. An internal probe of `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_sxt` during a chosen MOV, logical, add, or shift operation reveals R4 directly or as a known reversible function. The observation bypasses direct protection of R4; even a one-bit flag leaks a predicate that can be accumulated over chosen operations.
